summary.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One paleographic interpretation reads its ancient graph as a handled container and proposes that it was borrowed for ‘use’ through sound similarity; because the container’s spoken name is unknown, that match cannot be verified.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One interpretation treats the whole graph as a pictograph of a container, with its body on the left and handle on the right. The received 說文 account parses it as 卜 plus 中. Other accounts relate 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph, or describe 用 as 同 with a handle added and 同 as phonetic. The evidence does not settle these analyses or establish an internal sound component.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a handled bucket or container, with its body on the left and handle on the right. On this account, the graph was later reused for ‘put into effect/use’ through a proposed sound similarity; the container’s spoken name is unknown, so the match cannot be verified.

history.text: A form catalogue indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script and 說文 forms, but its text does not describe individual strokes or establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.

The container interpretation differs from the received 說文 parsing 從卜從中. Other accounts relate 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph; another describes 用 as 同 with a handle added and assigns 同 a sound role. These analyses remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘put into effect/use’ cannot be tested phonetically because the depicted object’s spoken name is unknown. 用’s own reconstructed readings do not establish that missing name or a sound match.

Oracle-bone examples attest 用 in contexts indicating whether a proposed action was carried out, but the first occurrence and relative chronology of this use and the proposed container sense are unsettled. A Qin-slip container or measure use read 桶 does not determine their order.

senses.text: 用/不用 is reported after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. This attested use does not establish the graph’s original meaning.
One Qin-slip context is read 桶, ‘container’ or ‘measure.’ It preserves a container-related use but does not establish the graph’s original meaning or when this use arose.

senses.gloss: preposition equivalent to 以; sequential or causal conjunction
senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples include prepositional and conjunctive uses alongside the verb ‘use.’ The examples do not establish their relative chronology or development.
用 has the current meaning ‘use’ or ‘employ.’ The evidence does not establish a complete path from the attested inscriptional uses to its present range.

limitations.text: Several uses are attested, but the evidence does not establish a semantic development linking them. The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘carry out/use’ lacks a verifiable sound match because the pictured object’s spoken name is unknown.

overview.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One interpretation says its ancient container picture may have been borrowed for ‘use’ because of a proposed sound similarity; the container’s spoken name is unknown, so the match is unverified.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a handled container; its spoken name is unknown, so the proposed sound-based borrowing for ‘use’ cannot be verified.

relationships.text: 用/不用 is reported after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. This attested use does not establish the graph’s original meaning.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: For bronze inscriptions, the database records 用 as a verb ‘use’, as a preposition equivalent to 以, and as a conjunction with sequential or causal senses, citing examples including 召仲鬲, 虢季子白盤, 守宮盤 and 禹鼎. search_audit.outcome: Inspected the 用 entry and its linked 同 entry. CUHK describes a graphic differentiation relationship; the separate 同 entry does not establish 同 as a phonetic component in 用.

gaps: The bucket interpretation is a scholarly paleographic analysis reported by the CUHK database, not a visually verified reading made in this research. The database links the graph form to 合集19762 and 21405, but no inscription facsimile was opened or independently assessed.

No securely dated first occurrence for the noun ‘bucket’ or the verb ‘use’ was established. The cited oracle-bone contexts support early use of the graph in a ‘carried out/not carried out’ formula, while the claim that the graph’s original referent was a bucket remains an interpretation.

The dossier’s account that 用 is a phonetic loan is not independently demonstrated by the pages inspected. The available inscriptional evidence supports graph borrowing from a proposed container pictograph for ‘put into effect/use’; it does not independently recover the depicted object’s spoken name or establish a sound match. No original bucket/tool name is identified, so no pronunciation comparison for that object is possible.

The dossier’s Wiktionary analysis of 同 as phonetic and its Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparisons were not confirmed by the consulted primary-oriented sources. The inspected CUHK page instead reports 用 and 同 as graphic variants/a divided graph; no phonetic-component reading comparison was warranted or established.
No component sound array was provided because the inspected evidence did not establish an internal sound component for 用. The local Baxter–Sagart and Unihan rows concern 用 itself only.
The official Unicode Unihan URL for U+7528 was attempted but inaccessible through the web tool. Consequently the local Unihan kMandarin row is not externally click-through verified.
No source reuse/license terms for the character-specific databases were inspected; no extract or bulk reuse is recommended from this research.
The bucket interpretation remains an attributed paleographic analysis; no oracle-bone facsimile was independently opened or visually assessed.

The exact first occurrence and absolute dating of the bucket/container sense and the ‘put into effect/use’ sense remain unsettled. Oracle-bone examples support the latter use, while Qin-slip evidence preserves 用 read 桶 in a measure context; this does not establish chronology by itself.

The proposed whole-graph borrowing account cannot be tested phonetically: no recoverable spoken name or pronunciation for the pictured bucket/object was established. Mandarin or reconstructed pronunciation of 用 does not establish the depicted object's name.

The dossier’s separate analysis of 用 as 同 plus a handle, with 同 acting phonetically, conflicts with the inspected CUHK account. No suitable component sound comparison was established, so no component sound array is provided.

The received 說文 analysis 從卜從中 is present in the dossier, while the inspected CUHK entry quotes 說文’s gloss and reports a later graphic-differentiation account involving 同. The inspected pages do not adjudicate the textual/paleographic disagreement.
Modern 用 kMandarin yòng is available in the supplied local row, but the official Unicode page was inaccessible; the third-party mirror is not the required official verification.

The Commons file description surfaced in search results, but the exact description page could not be opened, and its rights statement points to a separate permission agreement. Xiaoxuetang’s inspected rights notice does not grant CC0 reuse. No glyph image is selected because a verified usable image URL and reuse provenance were not obtained.
The CUHK character entry was used as a concise paraphrased, character-specific citation; no corpus-wide extract or bulk reuse terms were verified. No local extract is recommended.

limitations.text: No helpful glyph image is available here to show the proposed bucket-and-handle interpretation: the form catalogue does not supply an image with verified reuse permission, and the seal-script image’s source and permission terms remain unverified. The bucket reading is an attributed paleographic interpretation, not a visible form that can be checked against an image here.
